language.script_notes: Coastal (costeño) accent and vocabulary distinct from the interior, though not usually reflected in formal signage.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Less common given flatter coastal terrain.
road_furniture.curb_style: Colonial-era cobblestone streets within Cartagena's walled old town.

architecture.roof_style: Colonial tile roofs within historic Cartagena; simpler corrugated metal roofing common elsewhere along the coast given the heat.
architecture.roof_material: Terracotta tile in colonial old towns; corrugated metal widespread elsewhere.
architecture.wall_construction: Cartagena's UNESCO-listed walled old town is defined by colourful colonial Spanish architecture — pastel-painted buildings with wooden balconies and bougainvillea; simpler concrete-block construction in Barranquilla and smaller coastal towns.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Vivid pastel colours (yellow, blue, pink, orange) on Cartagena's colonial buildings is the region's strongest visual tell.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Cartagena's walled colonial old town with its fortifications and pastel buildings; Barranquilla's more modern port-city development; beach resort architecture further along the coast (Santa Marta).

nature.vegetation: Tropical coastal vegetation — palm trees, mangroves near river deltas and lagoons; drier scrub inland toward the Guajira Peninsula in the far northeast.
nature.terrain: A warm, humid Caribbean coastline with Cartagena's protected bay and historic fortifications; the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta rises dramatically and unusually close to the coast just east of Santa Marta.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid, tropical Caribbean climate year-round — bright coastal light and lush palm-lined streets.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heavy tourist/rental vehicle presence in Cartagena specifically.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Good coverage in Cartagena and Barranquilla given their tourism and port importance.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense along the coast and in the main coastal cities; sparser inland toward the Guajira Peninsula.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar tropical Caribbean coastal architecture and vegetation, both former Spanish colonial territories
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Colombia's yellow plates and Carrera/Calle grid signage differ from Panama's; Cartagena's specific fortified-wall colonial architecture is a unique regional landmark not replicated in Panama.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Caribbean coast is hot, humid and tropical with colourful colonial architecture; the Andean interior is cool and mountainous with coffee farms, and the Amazon/Llanos is flat lowland savanna or dense rainforest — all visually distinct.
